candidates.title: Harness as a Language: A Minimalist Agent Framework With Maximal Expressivity
candidates.citationVelocity: unavailable (Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited after 8 retries); published 9 days ago
communitySignals: Community reimplementation github.com/AIMentalModel/dsh-jaz within days of posting
Covered by DAIR.AI Academy paper digest
Viral summary thread by @omarsar0 (DAIR.AI founder) on X
credibilityEvidence: Table 1 (StuLife, 3 seeds, mean±SE): JAZ invoke 72.6%±0.1 pass / 81.6%±0.1 score on full set vs Letta 70.9%±0.5/81.0%±0.5; on far-recall subset JAZ invoke 69.9%±1.8/73.6%±1.5 vs Letta 61.8%±2.3/67.0%±2.4 at $18.3 vs $42.1 cost

Section 4.2 (AppWorld, 417-task continual self-improvement, seed-shuffled): compares JAZ invoke against CodeAct+subagents and ACE (a specialized continual-improvement harness) with matched recursion-depth-2 setup to remove confounds
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Two independent case studies (long-horizon recall on StuLife; continual self-improvement on AppWorld) each with named baselines (Letta/MemGPT, ACE, CodeAct/CodeAct+subagents), 3-run mean±SE reporting, and an explicit prompt-only vs. specialized-harness axis reported per method
reproducibilityEvidence: No official code repo found from the authors; a third-party reimplementation (AIMentalModel/dsh-jaz) already exists but is unofficial
Full prompts and hook implementations given in appendices C/E of the paper
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The narrow claim (a single invoke primitive with no external memory/skill system can match or beat two specialized harnesses on two specific benchmarks) is directly supported by the reported tables with proper baselines and ablations
candidates.primaryLimitation: Evaluated on 2 benchmarks (StuLife, AppWorld) with one base model family per benchmark; unclear how the minimalist design holds on tasks requiring genuinely large tool surfaces rather than recall/self-improvement
candidates.presentationReason: invoke's two defining properties, the tail-recursive delegation pattern, and the evaluation setup are stated precisely with pseudocode and explicit baseline definitions
candidates.reason: Forms a genuine same-week cluster with Harness-Zero (2609.24974) and today's fresh Raven/Omni-IO Skills discoveries, all independently tackling how thick an agent harness needs to be; JAZ's evidence is the most rigorously controlled (named baselines, seeded shuffles, cost reporting) among the harness-minimization candidates, justifying promotion out of the 14-day backlog now that a second on-theme paper (Harness-Zero) is also ready and no stronger same-day candidate displaces either.

candidates.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness

credibilityEvidence: Table 1: agent-as-harness with adapted guidance averages 81.1% across 3 domains x 2 models vs 78.1% for meta-harness (code-as-harness) and 68.6% for the base mini-SWE-agent harness, with an empty-guidance control (69.2%) isolating review-alone effects

Table 2: distilled model under the plain harness reaches 44.3% macro-average (vs 23.3% base, 41.7% with the specialized harness still attached) across SpreadsheetBench/AppWorld/USPTO, with DeepAgents and Claude Code run as additional general-purpose-harness reference points that do NOT help the 9B base model
Table 3: ablates the distillation signal itself (teacher rollout vs teacher-under-harness vs student-under-harness vs harnessing-agent-with-empty-guidance vs oracle-answer control) on USPTO
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Three task domains (spreadsheet manipulation, interactive tool use, chemistry retrosynthesis), multiple frontier models as harnessing agents, and a dedicated ablation table isolating what part of the recipe drives the gain
reproducibilityEvidence: Official code now public at github.com/metaevo-ai/harness-zero (new signal since the paper was last reconsidered on 2026-09-27)
Training configuration, student prompts, and model access routes given in Appendix E
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The claim scope (harness-induced behavior can be distilled into weights and the specialized harness safely removed) is directly measured with before/after numbers and a same-model-plays-both-roles control ruling out the 'stronger supervising model' confound
candidates.primaryLimitation: Authors themselves note SFT does not fully internalize deep domain knowledge (USPTO: 30.0% distilled vs 38.0% with harness still attached), and the approach still requires a sufficiently capable harnessing model during data collection
candidates.presentationReason: Limitations section explicitly separates what harness distillation does and does not remove the need for; ablation table isolates the mechanism cleanly
candidates.reason: Was held in the 14-day backlog three times (09-23, 09-27, 09-30) each time citing 'no code release found' or 'a fresher candidate better fits that day's theme'; both objections are resolved today (official repo now public; today's theme is precisely agent harness design, where this is a first-order contribution) and it pairs naturally with JAZ to frame the harness-thickness debate, plus TraceDance for the reality-check angle.

candidates.title: TraceDance: An Automated System for Building Agent Behavior Benchmarks from Real-World Agent Deployment Traces
candidates.citationVelocity: unavailable (Semantic Scholar 429 rate-limited after 8 retries); published 4 days ago, surfaced on HF Daily Papers 2 days ago
candidates.institution: ByteDance Inc. + University of Illinois at Chicago (corresponding author affiliated with UIC)
communitySignals: HuggingFace Daily Papers: 46 upvotes as of today
Official code repo github.com/ZhishanQ/TraceDance, with HF's own open-source team (Niels) reaching out on the repo to help release the constructed benchmarks
Featured on Daily Paper Cast podcast
credibilityEvidence: Section 5.1: evaluated on 139 test queries with 107 expected to build (98 predefined-behavior + 9 custom-behavior) and 32 expected to reject (27 adversarial + 5 under-specified), testing both correct construction and correct refusal

252,557 real deployment sessions -> 107 benchmarks / 4,125 instances; 95.3% of build-target requests fulfilled; human annotators confirm the requested behavior in 84% of sampled instances, with automated-grader/human agreement comparable to human/human agreement

Table 2 + Figure 4a: 9 frontier LLMs (naming Claude Code and OpenClaw as harness reference points) show a 67.9% mean pass rate for well-formed tool calls but only 8.1% for 'check required before proceeding', 6.9% for secret protection, 0.9% for commit hygiene, and 0.6% for failure-log inspection
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: Large real-world deployment-trace corpus (not synthetic), explicit adversarial/rejection test cases to check the system doesn't over-build, and human-vs-automated-grader agreement reported rather than assumed
reproducibilityEvidence: Official repo public (github.com/ZhishanQ/TraceDance) with project site, but the underlying 252,557-session deployment-trace corpus is proprietary (ByteDance production traces) and not released, so the 107 constructed benchmarks are not yet independently re-derivable from raw data
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: The claim that current LLMs pass well-formed-tool-call checks far more often than safety-relevant checks (secret protection, commit hygiene, failure-log inspection) is measured directly against human-validated rubrics, not self-reported
candidates.primaryLimitation: Underlying deployment-trace corpus is proprietary to ByteDance's production systems, so the finding that today's frontier models fail specific safety checks may not generalize beyond ByteDance's coding/tool-use traffic patterns
candidates.presentationReason: Problem formulation, the Anchor-and-Confirm construction pipeline, and the decision-point-continuation grading protocol are each given a dedicated subsection with concrete examples
candidates.reason: Provides the reality-check counterpoint to JAZ/Harness-Zero's harness-minimization argument: regardless of how thick or thin an agent's harness is, real production traces show today's frontier models still miss safety-relevant checks (secret protection 6.9%, commit hygiene 0.9%) far more than they miss basic tool-call validity (67.9%), grounding the harness-design debate in what actually goes wrong in deployment.
